name: Rowan Hale
about:
I make instruments for people who can't afford instruments. I came to SDIT for a better job and found out I liked finishing things more than I liked the job. Four years later: a surfboard with the maths to defend it, a logger that lived on the pier, a tide clock on a café counter, and a forty-dollar sensor that three strangers built from my guide and got the same numbers the four-thousand-dollar one gets.

Design concentration. The Cove is my lab. I want the work here to say one thing: cheap, honest, checked, and left where people can use it.
note: A sample portfolio. Rowan Hale is a fictional learner, written to show what four years of answers and made things look like here. Nothing on this page belongs to a real person.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: Getting a degree so I can get a better job. Honestly that's most of it. Maybe also proving to myself I can finish something.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: An app, probably. Something people use.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That you're either a math person or you're not, and I'm not.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: My phone at night. The mast is leaving it in the kitchen, which I did for a week. I slept better and missed nothing.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: The tide line on the steps at the Cove. It keeps getting closer to the next step and never quite touches it before it turns.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: I pushed off the wall in the pool and the wall pushed me across the lane. It didn't feel like the wall did anything.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Text me the buoy reading at 6 a.m. so I know whether to bother.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: A paper airplane that flies straight. It took eleven tries and throwing away the first ten without arguing with myself.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Losing the job at the shop. It looked like a loss. It's the reason I have time for this.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Played a voice memo at double speed. The pitch went up an octave. Same sound, half the time, twice the frequency.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Black's sand burned, the water was cold. Same sun. Water takes more energy to warm up, which is why the marine layer happens.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: 1101 plus 0111. The carry ran all the way to the left and made a fifth bit. Twenty.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Whisper. A room loses it at ten feet. The phone keeps every breath.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: The company owns it. I read the contract. Locke would have had questions.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Paint: three tubes and white. The screen: red, green, blue. My grandmother's spices, which is a stretch.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: "I think that it is probably important to note that" became nothing. That third was me being afraid to say it.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: A word in my notes. I used to search the whole file. Now the program jumps straight to it.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: A shelf I built got used as a step stool. I went back and made it stronger instead of telling them to stop.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Whether the 7:10 bus is late. It's late more than half the time. About 60 out of 100 before I'd stop calling it chance.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: "Four out of five surfers prefer" on a wax ad. Out of how many? It didn't say. I looked. Thirty.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Choosing a wave: I weigh the size, the crowd, and my mood, and then I weigh how much to trust the mood.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: The wiring on the carburetor job. Nobody else wanted it, so I took it.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: If it surprised me in a way it couldn't have been told to. I haven't seen it yet.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: The barista at the café on Newport. She'll meet it on the counter at 7 a.m. with no time.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: My fin box was cast. You can see the seam where the mold closed.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: A trick at the bowl that only exists because someone filmed it and the others copied it.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: "This sensor makes it cheap to watch the coast, and cheap to watch the people on it."

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: I assumed the salt was the enemy. It was the cable chafing on the piling. I noticed in week four.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: The pier mount. It held through two storms, so I stopped looking. The bracket had rusted halfway through.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: The Colorado, mostly, by way of an aqueduct I've never seen.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: I asked a model to clean my sensor data and didn't write down what it removed. I wrote it down after.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: The rule that the kelp grows toward the light, and the choice of which forty out of four thousand to keep.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: A coastal temperature and tide sensor anyone can build for forty dollars. It's done when three people who aren't me build one and their numbers match the pier's.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: That I'd been wrong on Day 0 and I was glad I wrote it down.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: A window, north, about the size of a door. It made my roommate's face look like a painting.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Five people: two scientists, a lifeguard, a teacher, and my mother. They saw three sensors agree with the pier to a tenth of a degree.

answers.heading: answer
answers.content: Said it to my roommate: the kit ships on the first of May. Then I shipped it.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: Less about the job than I thought. It's being able to look at something, a wave, a poem, a cup in a museum, and actually see it. I didn't know I couldn't.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: Something physical. I want to finish a board before summer.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That I'm not a math person. Less sure now. Calculus on a skate ramp is just paying attention.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: A three-minute film about my phone, a motion study of a drop-in, and a box of things I finished in the Workshop.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: I finish things. Day 1 said finishing was the assignment and I didn't believe it.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: Learning to make things that work and to say why they work. The board taught me more than any lecture: the numbers either hold water or they don't.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: A working computer from gates, which I didn't think was possible for me. And a better board.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That a sound is just a sum of waves. I can show it now.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: A 6'2" fish with the calculations to defend it, shown at the exhibition, and an eight-bit computer that runs my program.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: I stopped saying I'm not a math person.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: Practice being wrong in public and fixing it. Every essay came back marked. The marks were the education.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: Writing I'm not embarrassed by.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That the first draft is the real one. It isn't. The third is.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: Four essays with the drafts beside them, and a program that went from forty seconds to a fifth of a second.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: I read contracts now. And I cut a third of every sentence.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: Knowing what's true when someone is selling me something, including when I'm the one selling. And choosing a direction from what I've made, not what I imagined.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: Things people use. I declared Design.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That my judgment is better than chance. I scored my forecasts. It is, barely.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: Forty public swell forecasts, scored; a ninety-second film that went further than I expected; a carburetor rebuilt for a client.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: I want the numbers before I believe anything, my own ideas first.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: Learning who I'm making for. A thing nobody can use isn't finished.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: An instrument for people who can't afford instruments.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That scenes invent things before companies do. I watched it happen at the bowl.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: Tide Clock, a game in a café that strangers actually play, and a fin box that doesn't crack.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: I watch people use my work now instead of explaining it to them.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: The field term broke my idea that education happens in school. It's the habit of noticing what you assumed and checking it.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: The sensor, working, in the water, for a month.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That the thing that never failed is the thing you stopped checking.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: A temperature and tide logger that lived on the pier for five weeks, and a field report from twelve weeks at an instrument shop.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: I write down the result that contradicts me first.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: Taste and responsibility. The tools can make almost anything now. What's left is deciding what's worth making and owning it when it goes wrong.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: The capstone: a coastal sensor anyone can build for forty dollars.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That a machine can be my collaborator and the work still be mine, if I keep the ledger.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: A generative piece about kelp, with the rules on the wall, and a capstone proposal that survived the scoping.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: I keep a record of every handoff to a model, and I can say which calls were mine.

answers.heading: education
answers.content: On Day 0 I wrote that it was about a better job. I'd keep the part about finishing. The rest I'd cross out. Education is learning to see clearly, make things that hold up, and stand behind them in front of people. The job is a side effect.

answers.heading: make
answers.content: The company that builds the forty-dollar sensor for scientists who can't buy the four-thousand-dollar one.

answers.heading: believe
answers.content: That small scenes invent the future. I defended it in SIG 301 and I'd defend it again.

answers.heading: made
answers.content: The capstone, defended on the sand in front of five people who use it; a short film for the Crossing; a final build on the wall.

answers.heading: changed
answers.content: Almost everything I wrote on Day 0, except that I wanted to finish something.
